Its near perimeter has a shallow thickness band above a deeper horizontal board, with one square vertical member visible at the left. The far surface boundary is visible against the blue wall beside the printer; both slab ends and the boundary directly behind the body are concealed or cropped.
Width alignment — The printer’s front width boundaries rise gently toward its right. The slab’s long working edge and exposed far boundary run in the same general direction. Across the main front footprint, the working edge rises slightly more than the printer’s lower edge, so the exposed wood strip narrows modestly toward the printer’s right, apart from its rounded ends.

Physical dimensions cannot be recovered from these objects, and the slab’s total width is not visible.

The central output opening contains an inset ledge and a small projecting lip also visible in B. These printer recesses remain distinct from the wood below; exact underside contact points are hidden.
